The title Dreams allude to how life is so similar to dreams.

A rope grows erect from the crown of the head

An allusion to the crown chakra - the narrator is meditating. This sets the mood for the poem: in the first strophe we're caught in a moment of contemplation. The narrator is sensing external stimuli in a deep meditative state but the noises don't quite make sense to him. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahasrara

angels in the sky is taking an evening class on the skid pan

For example could be a noisy airplane flying by. In a detached state the sound of a motor roaring up in the sky makes very little sense and your mind begins to create abstract images (visions) of whatever input comes in, like:

A black swan hatches from a pebble.

Could be the sound of a bird mixed with the sound of a stone being tossed around or a vibration that conjures the image of the ground to the narrator.

I dream

In a state between sleep and awake he wonders how reality and dream are so similar in the way they are fantastic and offer endless possibilities.

that three times three is nine,

These thoughts go from hard science, in this case mathematics...

that the right-hand rule applies;

To pseudo-science, meta-physics, occultism or however you wanna call it https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left-hand_path_and_right-hand_path

when the circus leaves the trampled ground will once more overgrow with grass.

This could mean many things and is the intellectual and metaphoric climax of the poem. Some interpretations could be:

  1. After this moment is gone for the narrator and he leaves meditation he will forget all the things this moment is bringing him, even though it is so rich and resume his active routine, errands, work... The circus are those things around him.

  2. Could be a symbol of death: even if somehow mankind dies off the grass will still keep growing on it's own, or even if Earth and all life are destroyed all the planets and stars will still keep dancing around for billions of years. Or even if he himself died at that very moment all those other things happening around him will still go on. The circus is life itself, all the moving and breathing things that always seem so busy and entertained.

  3. While meditating one of the sounds coming in could be that of a circus, so this could be taken literally. The circus is a circus.
